newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mixed in featureless market.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mixed in featureless market.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed in a market void of any buying interest, traders said.

At the close, February RSS1 buyer was quoted at 298 cents ($1.20) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB), down half cent from Thursday. February SMR20 was unchanged at 293.50.

Traders could not report any overseas demand and said they expected the market to stay in the doldrums through the whole of the next fortnight when the twin Eid al-Fitr and Chinese New Year Lunar festivals take place.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 293 cents a kg, SMR CV at 356, SMR L at 336, SMR 5 at 304, SMR 10 at 294 and drum latex FOB at 233-234.
A dealer told Reuters that she expected the RRS1 and SMR20 to fall at least one or two cents next week to match up with cheaper rubber prices in Thailand and Indonesia.
The INRO five-day average was 230.39 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Jan 30 from 231.12 on Jan 29. The daily indicator was at 229.22 against 229.54 previously.
